R0017.title: Fake Transactions
R0017.description: Merchants complete large numbers of fake transactions to obtain platform merchant discounts/rebates, or to inflate product positive review counts at low cost. Methods generally include 'order A, ship B' schemes or directly shipping empty packages.
R0017.influence: Exploits platform merchant discounts/rebates. Enables unfair competition through inflated positive ratings.

references.title: Case Study: Operating a Money Laundering Platform for Cyber Black-Grey Market Merchants

observables: An abnormally high proportion of merchant orders use empty-package tracking numbers or fake logistics trajectories
'Order A, ship B' orders have shipping addresses concentrated at warehouse drop-ship points, with categories that do not match the ordered items
Self-purchased merchant orders show strong linkage between buyer and seller accounts, devices, and funds
Positive review rates spike in the short term but fulfillment evidence (logistics, delivery confirmation) is missing
Transactions concentrate during platform rebate or subsidy campaigns and drop sharply after the campaign ends

R0017-001.title: Order Brushing
R0017-001.definition: Merchants completing bulk low-cost or fake orders to inflate transaction volume or improve ratings.
R0017-001.description: Merchants complete large numbers of low-cost transactions to obtain platform merchant discounts/rebates, or to inflate product positive review counts at low cost. Methods generally include hiring buyers or maliciously listing low-value items to complete bulk transactions.
R0017-001.influence: Undermines fair competition principles on the platform; in some cases exploits platform merchant discounts/rebates.

references.title: Interim Provisions on Anti-Unfair Competition in Cyberspace

observables: Merchant order volume surges during campaigns, but fulfillment tracking numbers are duplicated or fake
Brushing buyer accounts share clustered registration times, sparse purchase histories, and templated reviews
Low-value items are ordered in bulk, with unit prices inverted against shipping costs
Buyer and seller accounts, shipping addresses, and payment accounts show correlated clustering
Positive reviews concentrate shortly after brushing is completed, with review content that does not match product characteristics

R0017-002.title: Subsidy Fraud
R0017-002.definition: Defrauding platform or government subsidies, rewards, or promotional funds through fabricated transactions, forged data, or other fraudulent means.
R0017-002.description: Exploiting loopholes in platform subsidy policies to claim subsidy funds that should not be obtained, through methods such as fake transactions, order brushing, or fabricating user activity. Common tactics include: hiring brushers to create fake transaction records; using multiple accounts to repeatedly claim subsidies; running ghost rides or fake orders on ride-hailing or food delivery platforms to defraud subsidies; e-commerce sellers buying from themselves to exploit platform merchant discounts and rebates.
R0017-002.influence: Causes financial losses to platforms and governments, undermines fair competition, and distorts market resource allocation.

references.title: Black Market Big Data: 2025 Global E-Commerce Fraud Risk Research Report
Hiring Order Brushers and Recruiting Insiders to Defraud E-Commerce Platform Subsidies: 9-Person Gang Caught

observables: Ride-hailing and food delivery platforms show large volumes of ghost-ride brushing with trip trajectories that do not match actual routes
Subsidy-claiming accounts cluster across multiple devices and phone numbers, repeatedly claiming the same subsidy
Newly registered accounts surge during subsidy campaigns and centrally trigger subsidy thresholds
Self-purchased merchant order amounts are precisely pinned at subsidy or rebate thresholds
After subsidy funds arrive, accounts rapidly withdraw and deregister, with fund flows highly concentrated

R0017-003.title: Merchant Cash-Out and Fake Transaction Fraud
R0017-003.definition: Merchants use fake orders, circular transactions, or abnormal refunds to cash out and transfer funds.
R0017-003.description:
Merchant cash-out and fake transaction fraud uses fake orders, circular transactions, linked accounts, or abnormal refunds to convert payment rails and platform subsidies into cash. Attackers may coordinate as merchants and buyers.

The fraud pollutes transaction data, increases payment channel risk, and may trigger anti-money-laundering obligations. Risk control needs to link merchants, buyers, devices, funds, and fulfillment evidence.
R0017-003.influence: Fake transactions cause subsidy and fee losses, increase payment channel risk, and may support cash-out or money laundering.

observables: Merchant orders show circular transactions or mutual payments among linked accounts, forming a closed fund-flow loop
The abnormal refund ratio is high, with refund amounts concentrating into a few linked accounts
Merchant and buyer device fingerprints, shipping addresses, and payment accounts show dense linkage
Transaction amounts frequently approach but do not exceed risk-control thresholds, exhibiting threshold-pinning characteristics
A large volume of equal-amount or multiple-amount orders is generated at the same merchant within a short window, followed by rapid refunds
